acceptance.given: A historical replay receipt is being produced from the repository-bound historical validator and command evidence.

oracle.expected: The receipt records the historical validator repository-relative path and SHA-256, and validation recomputes that SHA-256 from the referenced validator before accepting the replay.
forbidden: Accepting a historical replay without auditable validator identity evidence.
oracle.observable: The replay receipt's historical_validator object contains the validator path and matching SHA-256; a missing, unreadable, or hash-mismatched reference fails validation.

acceptance.then: Historical validator identity is independently recorded and validated as non-authorizing audit evidence.
acceptance.when: When recording or validating historical replay evidence.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Run the historical-replay identity assertion with a missing or SHA-256-drifted historical validator reference.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Make historical replay validation retain an auditable historical validator path and recomputed content identity, rejecting absent or drifted identity evidence while retaining historical evidence as non-authorizing.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Historical receipts remain non-authorizing; rollback removes only the added identity-validation behavior and does not rewrite historical evidence.

slice_hint.state_transition: Historical validator reference not independently recorded and validated -> historical validator path and SHA-256 are recorded and verified before replay acceptance.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The targeted tests prove that a replay receipt with the repository historical validator includes a matching auditable identity, while missing or drifted validator identity is rejected.

acceptance.given: A Consumer Manifest has non-empty entries and each applicable route transition has completed before rollback.

oracle.expected: Every non-empty Consumer Manifest entry observes the Prior Behavior Baseline after rollback.
forbidden: A non-empty Consumer Manifest entry does not observe the Prior Behavior Baseline after rollback.
oracle.observable: The aggregate replay result maps every non-empty Consumer Manifest entry to a completed applicable transition and a post-rollback Prior Behavior Baseline observation, with 100% coverage.

acceptance.then: Each non-empty Consumer Manifest entry observes the Prior Behavior Baseline after rollback.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Execute the Consumer Manifest rollback evaluation with one non-empty consumer lacking its post-rollback baseline observation.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Evaluate rollback results per non-empty Consumer Manifest entry and fail the aggregate when any applicable consumer route does not observe its Prior Behavior Baseline.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Rollback restores prior consumer behavior without rewriting the Consumer Manifest, replay evidence, or historical records.

slice_hint.state_transition: No post-rollback baseline observation is established -> every non-empty Consumer Manifest entry has a completed applicable transition and a Prior Behavior Baseline observation.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The aggregate is successful only when 100% of non-empty Consumer Manifest entries observe the Prior Behavior Baseline after rollback; one missing observation produces the expected red result.

acceptance.given: The Matrix evaluation is run against the defined six Matrix Cases and both subjects.

oracle.expected: Each of the six Matrix Cases executes exactly one input, and the six executed inputs are pairwise distinct.
forbidden: Two or more Matrix Cases use the same input.
A Matrix Case lacks an input execution.
oracle.observable: The Matrix aggregate contains six executed case records whose input identities are pairwise distinct; any missing execution or duplicate input fails the aggregate.

acceptance.then: All six Matrix Cases have executed distinct inputs for both subjects.
acceptance.when: When the Matrix evaluation is run.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Evaluate a six-case matrix containing either an unexecuted case or duplicate input identities.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Make matrix aggregation require six executed Matrix Cases for both subjects and reject missing execution records or reused input identities.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Rollback removes only matrix distinct-input enforcement and does not alter stored matrix definitions or historical evidence.

slice_hint.state_transition: Matrix Case execution coverage is unestablished -> six cases execute pairwise-distinct inputs across both subjects.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The matrix aggregate accepts only six executed records with pairwise-distinct inputs and rejects any missing execution or reused input.

acceptance.given: An adversarial validator case is submitted to success evaluation.

oracle.expected: The case receives a non-success result.
forbidden: Success is accepted for an adversarial validator case.
oracle.observable: The evaluation result for the adversarial validator case is non-success, and the aggregate cannot report success for that case.

acceptance.then: Success is rejected for the adversarial validator case.
acceptance.when: An adversarial validator case is evaluated.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Evaluate an adversarial validator case that would otherwise be marked successful and assert that success is rejected.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Ensure the toolchain evaluation pipeline classifies adversarial validator cases as non-success and prevents them from contributing a successful aggregate result.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Rollback restores prior evaluator behavior only; it does not alter validator capabilities, matrix inputs, or recorded evidence.

slice_hint.state_transition: An adversarial validator case is presented for success evaluation -> its evaluation result is non-success.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: A targeted adversarial-validator case cannot be accepted as success, and the aggregate reports non-success for that case.
